facts: Control channel is numeric zero. SPECIFIC is numeric zero; CONTROL is the bit-2 cross-service message-type tag, not synonymous with using channel zero.
VERSION_REQUEST, SSL_HANDSHAKE and AUTH_COMPLETE are channel0, PLAIN and SPECIFIC. BULK wrapping therefore has flags3, not7.
Version request is a 2-byte big-endian ID 1 then major/minor big-endian uint16, both1 in the pin. It is not a Protobuf message and not the AOA protocol query.

findings.classification: direct source with explicit portability limitation
facts: VERSION_RESPONSE has 2-byte ID2 plus major/minor uint16 BE and a 16-bit status word. The old parser treats insufficient words as default major/minor0 or MISMATCH rather than strict exact-length rejection.

The old source converts major/minor from BE but casts status directly; current pin defines only MATCH0 and MISMATCH0xffff so those constants are endian-invariant. Unknown statuses are not validated by this parser.
OpenAuto rejects only MISMATCH and does not enforce exact returned major/minor. Root strict exact-version/status policy would be a new local policy, not proven current-phone negotiation.
The old reinterpret_cast uint16 parsing is not a portable byte parser and should not be copied into new code.

SSL_HANDSHAKE message ID3 is followed by raw TLS BIO bytes, not a serialized handshake Protobuf. It remains AA-plaintext outer payload even though TLS records have their own internal encryption semantics.
AUTH_COMPLETE message ID4 wraps a proto2 message with required status field1; OK0 must be explicitly present. Empty body omitting the default zero is invalid for this pinned required field.

findings.classification: direct source observation; runtime occurrence remains untested here
facts: On doHandshake false OpenAuto drains outbound BIO via readHandshakeBuffer then sendHandshake. On true it directly enqueues AUTH_COMPLETE and never examines/drains pending handshake output in that branch.
Cryptor sets isActive immediately on local SSL_ERROR_NONE, before AUTH transport completion. The entity immediately requests another control receive after enqueueing output.

This proves absence of an explicit successful-handshake output-drain guard, not that the old ordinary TLS1.2 handshake loses a flight in every run. The selected client/peer handshake path can naturally have no final outbound bytes.

Cryptor recognizes WANT_READ and success; WANT_WRITE is treated as an error. SSLWrapper uses TLSv1_2_client_method for OpenSSL<1.1 but TLS_client_method for newer versions, so the pin alone cannot fix all future library protocol behavior.
findings.recommended_root_gate: After every TLS handshake drive, including success, preserve/drain all pending TX. Finish every ID3 transport fragment/completion before sending AUTH_COMPLETE. Mark app-ready only after AUTH send completion or under an explicitly documented weaker transport-ordered policy. This is stronger local engineering policy, not an official Pixel guarantee.

findings.classification: direct old ownership observation and new-port inference
facts: Messenger serializes message send queue and USBTransport handles partial sends until complete; enqueue alone is not physical successful send. Separate receive/send strands mean receive can advance while AUTH is queued.

Transport/DataSink owns remaining input, consumes exactly requested count into a new copied common::Data and retains all unread completion tail. No cold/post-handshake receiver replacement occurs in these reviewed source files: same MessageInStream and Cryptor continue.

A custom bootstrap handover must preserve any same-USB-completion tail, already copied pending wire frames, a partially collected next wire header/payload, and unconsumed TLS RX state. Local handshake success does not justify dropping those bytes.

Do not reset/reinit a live wire parser or recursively feed post-handshake receiver from within its callback. Handover through one serialized owner after the callback returns, or use exact consumed count and retained unconsumed tail.

Preserve the same authenticated TLS session: do not reinitialize TLS at receiver handover or feed the same ciphertext twice. A LAST plaintext fragment accepted before message backpressure stays accepted; retry complete owned message, not ciphertext/fragment.
SERVICE_DISCOVERY_RESPONSE is ENCRYPTED+SPECIFIC. ControlServiceChannel receive dispatches by 2-byte ID rather than using CONTROL flag to select this channel.
Old PingRequest is PLAIN+SPECIFIC and pinger scheduling begins at startup before version exchange. Do not infer all control-channel messages must become encrypted after AUTH.

Current Pixel/Android Auto version format extensions, accepted cert/profile/TLS behavior, sequencing, permitted flags or minimum channels remain unverified. Both commits are older implementation references, not an official Google specification.
